clue.text: Japanese film idol's worse on the radio

indicators.note: words heard broadcast are judged by sound alone, so the spelling can change

parts.note: an idol is a god, and iller is a colloquial comparative of ill, so idol's worse is god's iller

explanation.surface: A Japanese pop idol sounds poorly in a radio interview.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'god's iller' runs together into the monster's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Godzilla is the 1954 Japanese monster movie, the first of a long franchise.

clue.text: All the best cargo leaked

parts.note: goods are freight carried as cargo
peed is slang for urinated, a crude kind of leaking

explanation.surface: A send-off wish for a ship whose cargo has leaked.
explanation.definitionFit: Godspeed, or good speed, is a farewell wishing someone success on their way.

clue.text: Generators turning such a lot died

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

indicators.note: turning means the phrase for such a lot is reversed

parts.note: so many is another way of saying such a lot

explanation.surface: So many generators were turning that something died.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a machine that generates electric current.

clue.text: Nomad wearing dry clothes, the reflective type

parts.note: to be in something is to be wearing it

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the letters for dry dress the nomad

parts.note: TT means teetotal, abstaining from drink
a rover is a wanderer

explanation.surface: A wandering traveller in dry clothes is a thoughtful sort.
explanation.walkthrough: Clothes reads as a noun but works as a verb, wrapping one piece in another.
explanation.definitionFit: An introvert is inward-looking, given to reflection rather than socialising.

clue.text: League sorry to report spy found things

indicators.note: sorry means wretched or poor, so the letters following are in a sorry state

explanation.surface: A league official is sorry to report that a spy found some things.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost property is the collective name for items left behind and handed in after being found.

clue.text: Camilla finally waves too

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the name Camilla

parts.note: the last letter of the name Camilla
a swell is a long rolling movement of sea waves

explanation.surface: Queen Camilla at last gives a royal wave as well.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an everyday synonym for also, adding something further.

clue.text: United supporters turned up in disarray

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: fans support a team

explanation.surface: Manchester United's fans turn up in a chaotic state.
explanation.definitionFit: Snafu is military slang for a chaotic mess, a situation in total disorder.

clue.text: Scholarly university dons tried out Ecstasy

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so the university letter is clothed in the other letters
out means the letters are put out of their original order

explanation.surface: Learned university dons have experimented with Ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Dons looks like academics but is a verb, to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudite means learned, showing great knowledge acquired through study.

clue.text: Money that's funnyish?

parts.note: British slang for money, and split up it reads as LOL, laugh out loud, with an -ly ending, as if meaning a bit funny

explanation.walkthrough: Lolly is British slang for cash; split up, it looks like LOL with a -ly ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolly is informal British slang for money, as in raking in the cash.

clue.text: Most fancy golden buns buttery in the middle

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
buns is slang for buttocks, and nates is the anatomical word for them

indicators.note: in the middle asks for the central letter of the seven-letter word buttery

parts.note: the fourth of seven letters, the middle of buttery

explanation.surface: A bakery boasts its fanciest golden buns are buttery in the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The buns are not baked goods but buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, so the superlative is the most elaborate or showy.

clue.text: Easygoing American state holding the country back

indicators.note: holding means the state's letters wrap around the other piece

parts.note: CAL is a short form for California

indicators.note: back means the letters for the country are read in reverse order

parts.note: in an American context the country is the USA

explanation.surface: A laid-back US state is accused of holding the nation back.
explanation.walkthrough: California's abbreviation here is CAL rather than the postal CA.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual describes a relaxed, informal manner, the same as an easygoing one.

clue.text: Lucky golfer perhaps, playing against twin with no clubs

parts.note: a pro is a professional, such as a golfer

indicators.note: with no tells us to drop the letter for clubs from the twin word

parts.note: an identical is an identical twin
C stands for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A golfer is fortunate to play against a twin who has no clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Clubs suggests golf clubs; it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Providential means happening by good fortune, as if arranged by providence.

clue.text: Result of wrestling without the ring

indicators.note: without tells us to remove the ring-shaped letter from the wrestling word

parts.note: sumo is the Japanese style of wrestling
the letter O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: The outcome of a wrestling bout fought with no ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Sumo is fought in a ring, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is the total, the outcome of adding numbers together.

clue.text: Window half open left by agreement

indicators.note: half says only the first two of the four letters of open are used

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
unity is agreement, being of one mind

explanation.surface: A window left partly ajar, agreed on by everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Window' looks like part of the house, but it is the definition, as in a window of opportunity.
explanation.definitionFit: A window is a brief chance or interval in which something can be done, an opportunity.

clue.text: Follow indomitable US newshound going around jails

indicators.note: going around means the captured letters are read in the reverse direction
jails means the answer's letters are locked up inside the phrase's run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of indomitable, all of US and the start of newshound

explanation.surface: A dogged American reporter follows a story by touring prisons.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after, as a consequence or in sequence.

clue.text: Lobes very wrinkly on the side you can see

definitions.text: on the side you can see

indicators.note: wrinkly suggests something crumpled and folded out of its original shape

explanation.surface: A description of brain lobes, deeply wrinkled on their visible face.
explanation.definitionFit: The obverse is the front face of a coin or object, so obversely means on the visible facing side.

clue.text: Space transmitter starts to relay rubbish including 'So long and thanks …'

indicators.note: including means those two letters hold the farewell words between them
starts to asks for the opening letter of each of relay and rubbish

parts.note: the opening letters of relay and rubbish
adios is Spanish for goodbye
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A space probe relays junk, signing off So long and thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: The quote nods to Douglas Adams's So Long, and Thanks for All the Fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio star is a celestial object emitting strong radio waves, a source in space.

clue.text: Flexible goal as yet for exercise regime

indicators.note: flexible means bendable, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A flexibility goal not yet reached in a fitness programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogalates is a workout combining yoga and Pilates.

clue.text: Fellow books place in hospital, receiving new warning of fragility

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

indicators.note: receiving means the hospital place takes the letter for new inside it

parts.note: a patient is given a bed in hospital

explanation.surface: A college fellow books a hospital bed and is handed a fresh health warning.
explanation.definitionFit: The words are printed on envelopes and parcels whose contents could be damaged by folding.

clue.text: Fools in flannel lie still

indicators.note: in signals the answer is contained within the run of words that follow

parts.note: the answer runs from the end of flannel through lie into the start of still

explanation.surface: Idiots lying motionless wrapped in flannel.
explanation.walkthrough: A nelly is British slang for a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: Nellies are foolish or feeble people, in informal British use.

clue.text: Get to work in IT

parts.note: read as making faulty code run in computing, where faults are called bugs, not setting off to an office tech job

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like starting the working day in an office tech department, but it means making faulty code run.
explanation.definitionFit: To debug is to find and remove errors from software so it functions.

clue.text: Roll over and die, a retiree's expectation?

indicators.note: over means the roll word is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: a sub is a submarine sandwich, a long bread roll
to pass is to die, as in pass away

explanation.surface: Rolling over and dying, as if that is all a retiree can expect.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain pensioners get a free bus pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Older people in the UK are entitled to a free travel card for local buses.

clue.text: Slowing down on land and later at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ship slows down on land and later out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The on land/at sea contrast is the surface; the musical sense of the answer is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallentando is the musical direction for a gradual decrease in tempo.

clue.text: King and queen between them having one bicycle

indicators.note: the two royal letters together hold the word for one in the middle

parts.note: an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: A king and queen sharing just one bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A racer is a lightweight bicycle built for speed.

clue.text: Avoid capsizing in English Channel

indicators.note: capsizing turns things upside down, so in this down entry the letters run from bottom to top

parts.note: Dave is a British television channel

explanation.surface: Trying not to capsize while crossing the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: English Channel suggests the sea strait; Dave is a UK TV channel.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to escape or dodge something.

clue.text: Capital of Peru implying Lima; …

definitions.note: capital here means money, the Peruvian currency

parts.note: so introduces a conclusion, as in thus or therefore
Lima is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for L

explanation.surface: A geography question: Peru's capital, which implies Lima.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital looks like the seat of government, which would be Lima; it means money.
explanation.definitionFit: The sol is the currency unit of Peru, and capital means funds.

clue.text: … capital of Chile the same? Wrong conclusion

indicators.note: capital means the initial letter of the following word Chile

parts.note: the opening letter of the country name
the same refers back to Lima in the previous clue
a cross mark, X, shows an answer is wrong

explanation.surface: Is Chile's capital also Lima? That would be a wrong conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link this to the previous clue, whose Lima the same refers to.
explanation.definitionFit: A climax is the culminating point or final high point of events.

clue.text: Amuse police officer with wiles around court

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the word for wiles back to front

parts.note: arts are cunning tricks or wiles

explanation.surface: A police officer's cunning tricks keep everyone entertained in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To distract can mean to divert, entertaining someone so they forget their cares.

clue.text: More extravagant slice

definitions.meaning: first meaning: more reckless, the comparative of rash
second meaning: a thin slice of bacon

explanation.walkthrough: One word is both an adjective comparing recklessness and a noun for a bacon strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash means hasty and imprudent; separately, a rasher is a cut of bacon.

clue.text: Ask sir curiously about empty local comprehensive

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the emptied word
curiously means oddly, so the letters are set in an odd order
empty strips out the inner letters of local, leaving just its ends

parts.note: the word local emptied of its middle leaves just its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A parent quizzes the head of the local comprehensive school, which is strangely deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: Comprehensive looks like a British state school; it describes insurance cover.
explanation.definitionFit: All-risks insurance covers every form of loss, so it is comprehensive cover.
